title: Zeroth-Order Optimization of Optical Neural Networks with Linear Combination Natural Gradient and Calibrated Model
problem: Standard neural network training schemes perform poorly for optical neural networks due to their special parameterization and fabrication variations. Existing zeroth-order optimization methods struggle with ONN-specific challenges.
motivation: Optical neural networks offer low energy consumption and high-speed processing, making improved training methods essential for practical deployment.
method: The paper improves zeroth-order optimization (training by testing different parameter settings rather than computing mathematical gradients, which is difficult for optical hardware) for optical neural networks. It combines two key advances: linear combination natural gradient, which accounts for how optical network parameters interact uniquely and uses this knowledge to guide the search, and calibration-based direction vectors that generate smart search directions based on measurements of the actual optical system rather than guessing randomly. Both techniques keep computational cost low, making it practical to train optical neural networks efficiently.
key_novelty: Combining linear combination natural gradient with calibration-based direction vectors enables efficient training of optical neural networks without needing to compute gradients.
contributions: Linear combination natural gradient to address ONN parameterization challenges
Calibrated direction vector generation for improved zeroth-order optimization
Experimental validation showing significant improvements over existing ZO methods with minimal overhead

metrics.other: Significantly outperforms existing zeroth-order optimization methods

primary_theme: Training optimization for optical neural networks
